tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.does: General AI assistant: chat, writing, analysis, images, voice, web search and agents.
pros: Large ecosystem of GPTs and integrations
cons: Best features need a paid plan

tools.name: Claude
tools.does: AI assistant strong at writing, analysis, long documents and coding.
cons: Fewer built-in media tools than some rivals

tools.name: Gemini
tools.does: Google's AI assistant, connected to Search, Gmail, Docs and YouTube.
cons: Integration value depends on using Google apps

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.does: AI assistant in Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft apps.
cons: Office integration needs a Microsoft 365 plan
Several Copilot brands can be confusing

tools.name: Grok
tools.does: AI assistant integrated with X (Twitter), with real-time post search.
cons: Closely tied to the X platform

tools.name: Meta AI
tools.does: AI assistant inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, built on Llama.
pros: Free and inside apps people already use

tools.name: DeepSeek
tools.does: Chat app and low-cost API for DeepSeek's open-weight reasoning models.
cons: Data stored in China may not suit some organizations

tools.name: Le Chat
tools.does: Mistral's assistant with web search, documents and code.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.does: AI answer engine that searches the web and cites its sources.
cons: Quality depends on the sources it finds
Advanced modes need a paid plan

tools.name: Kimi
tools.does: AI assistant known for long-context reading and open-weight models.

tools.name: Qwen Chat
tools.does: Chat app for Alibaba's Qwen models, many of them open-weight.
cons: Smaller app ecosystem in the West

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.does: Research notebook that answers only from the documents you upload, and makes audio overviews.
pros: Answers grounded in your own sources
cons: Limited to the sources you add

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.does: Agentic coding tool in the terminal and IDEs: reads code, edits files, runs commands and tests.
pros: Handles multi-step tasks end to end
Extensible with skills, plugins and MCP
cons: Usage costs can grow on big tasks

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.does: AI pair programmer in VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub: completions, chat and coding agent.
pros: Works in the most popular editors

tools.name: Cursor
tools.does: AI-first code editor (VS Code-based) with chat, multi-file edits and agents.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.does: Coding agent in the terminal (open-source CLI), IDE and cloud.
tools.cost: Included with ChatGPT plans or API
pros: Can run tasks in the cloud
cons: Best experience needs a paid plan

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.does: Open-source AI agent for the terminal, powered by Gemini.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.does: AI code editor with an agent that plans and edits across files.

tools.name: Aider
tools.does: AI pair programming in the terminal that edits files and commits to git.
pros: Open source, works with many models
cons: You pay for the model API

tools.name: Replit Agent
tools.does: Builds and deploys full apps in the browser from a prompt.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.does: Creates web apps from chat, with a database and deployment.

tools.name: v0
tools.does: Generates React and Next.js user interfaces and apps from prompts.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.does: Builds, runs and deploys full-stack web apps in the browser from prompts.
cons: Larger projects get harder to manage

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.does: Generates artistic, high-quality images from text prompts.
cons: Less precise with text in images

tools.name: GPT Image (in ChatGPT)
tools.does: Creates and edits images by chatting in ChatGPT or through the API.

tools.name: Stable Diffusion
tools.does: Open image-generation models you can run locally or in apps.
tools.cost: Open models; paid API/licenses for some uses

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.does: Image and design generation built into Photoshop, Illustrator and Express.
pros: Inside Adobe tools designers already use

tools.name: FLUX
tools.does: Image-generation models, some open-weight, known for realism and prompt accuracy.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.does: Image generator known for accurate text inside images (logos, posters).

tools.name: Canva AI
tools.does: AI design tools in Canva: images, writing, presentations and editing.
pros: Templates plus AI in one place
cons: Best AI features on paid plans
Less control than pro design tools

tools.name: Sora
tools.does: Discontinued: OpenAI's text-to-video model. The Sora app and website closed on 26 April 2026 and the Sora API on 24 September 2026; OpenAI named no replacement. Kept here for reference.
cons: Use Veo, Kling or Runway instead

tools.name: Veo
tools.does: Google's video-generation model, available in Gemini, Flow and Vertex AI.

tools.name: Runway
tools.does: AI video generation and editing tools for creators.
pros: Many video tools in one place

tools.name: Kling
tools.does: Text- and image-to-video generation.

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.does: Creates presenter videos with AI avatars for training and communications.

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.does: AI avatar videos and video translation with lip-sync.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.does: Realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning and dubbing.

tools.name: Suno
tools.does: Generates songs with vocals from a text prompt.
cons: Commercial use needs a paid plan

tools.name: Whisper
tools.does: Open-source speech-to-text model for transcription and translation.
cons: No live meeting features by itself

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.does: Transcribes and summarizes meetings in Zoom, Teams and Google Meet.

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.does: AI meeting assistant: records, transcribes and summarizes calls.
cons: Bot joining calls can bother attendees

tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
tools.does: AI inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, grounded in your work data.
pros: Works across your Office files and mail
cons: Value depends on how well data is organized

tools.name: Gemini for Google Workspace
tools.does: Gemini inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides and Meet.

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.does: AI writing, search and Q&A across your Notion workspace.
pros: Searches all your notes and docs
Good for teams already on Notion
cons: Only as useful as your Notion content

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.does: AI writing assistant for grammar, tone and rewriting everywhere you type.
pros: Works in most apps and browsers

tools.name: Gamma
tools.does: Creates presentations, documents and web pages from a prompt.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.does: Hub for open models, datasets and demo apps (Spaces), plus the Transformers library.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.does: Open-source framework for building LLM apps and agents: models, prompts, tools, retrievers and many integrations. Part of the LangChain family with LangGraph and LangSmith.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.does: Framework for connecting LLMs to your data: ingestion, indexing and RAG.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.does: Runs open models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma and more) on your own computer with one command.
cons: Needs a capable GPU or Mac for big models
Slower than cloud for large models

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.does: Desktop app to download, chat with and serve local models.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.does: High-throughput engine for serving LLMs (PagedAttention, continuous batching).

tools.name: NVIDIA NIM
tools.does: Prebuilt, optimized containers for running AI models on NVIDIA GPUs.
tools.cost: Free to try; NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production

tools.name: PyTorch
tools.does: The most widely used deep-learning framework for research and production.

tools.name: TensorFlow
tools.does: Deep-learning framework with strong production and mobile tooling.
cons: Less popular than PyTorch for new research

tools.name: Weights & Biases
tools.does: Experiment tracking, model evaluation and LLM observability.

tools.name: Pinecone
tools.does: Managed vector database for semantic search and RAG.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.does: Open-source embedding database, easy to start with for RAG.
cons: Fewer enterprise features than managed options

tools.name: n8n
tools.does: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes; self-hostable.
cons: Complex flows get hard to maintain

tools.name: Zapier
tools.does: No-code automation across thousands of apps, with AI steps and agents.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock
tools.does: Managed access to many foundation models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Amazon Nova) with agents and RAG.

tools.name: Azure AI Foundry
tools.does: Build, evaluate and deploy AI apps and agents with OpenAI and other models on Azure.

tools.name: Google Vertex AI
tools.does: Google Cloud platform for Gemini and other models, training, tuning and MLOps.
pros: Full ML lifecycle in one place

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.does: One API to access hundreds of models from many providers.
cons: Extra hop between you and the provider

tools.name: Groq
tools.does: Very fast inference for open models on custom LPU chips, via API.

tools.name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
tools.does: Open protocol for connecting AI apps to tools and data sources.
pros: Write a tool once, use it in many AI apps
cons: Security of third-party servers must be checked

tools.name: Manus
tools.does: General AI agent that plans and carries out multi-step tasks: research, reports, slides, websites and data analysis.
pros: Handles long tasks end to end

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.does: Agent mode in the Claude desktop app that works with your files and apps to complete office tasks for you.
pros: Works on real files and folders

tools.name: OpenClaw
tools.does: Open-source personal AI agent you run yourself; it connects to chat apps and tools and can act on your behalf.

tools.name: Google Opal
tools.does: Google Labs tool for building and sharing small AI-powered mini apps from plain-language prompts, with no code.

tools.name: Base44
tools.does: Builds full web apps with a database, login and hosting from a text prompt.
pros: Fast from idea to working app

tools.name: CrewAI
tools.does: Python framework and platform for building teams of role-based AI agents that work together on tasks.

tools.name: Dify
tools.does: Open-source platform for building LLM apps, RAG chatbots and agent workflows with a visual editor.

tools.name: Pipecat
tools.does: Open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and multimodal AI agents.
pros: Works with many speech and LLM providers
cons: Real-time systems are complex to tune

tools.name: Postiz
tools.does: Open-source social media scheduler with AI help for writing posts, plus analytics across many networks.
pros: Many social networks in one place
Can be driven by AI agents
cons: Fewer features than big paid tools

tools.name: Harvey
tools.does: AI platform built for law firms and legal teams: research, drafting, contract review and regulatory tracking.

tools.name: Jobright
tools.does: AI job-search copilot that matches you to jobs, tailors your resume and helps you apply.

tools.name: Teal
tools.does: Resume builder and job tracker with AI to tailor resumes and cover letters to each job.
cons: Focused on the US job market

tools.name: Writesonic
tools.does: AI writing and SEO platform for blog posts, marketing copy and search visibility.

tools.name: Rytr
tools.does: Simple, low-cost AI writing assistant with templates for emails, ads and posts.
cons: Less capable than top chat assistants

tools.name: Sudowrite
tools.does: AI writing partner for fiction authors: brainstorming, describing scenes and drafting chapters.
pros: Keeps your story bible in context

tools.name: Lex
tools.does: Clean AI-assisted word processor for drafting, editing and getting feedback on writing.
cons: Fewer features than Google Docs or Word
Advanced models need a paid plan

tools.name: TinyWow
tools.does: Free website with many small tools: PDF conversion, image editing and AI writing helpers.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.does: Library for stateful, multi-step agents built as graphs of nodes and edges, with loops, memory, checkpoints and human-in-the-loop.
cons: Graph concepts take time to learn

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.does: Platform to trace, debug, evaluate and monitor LLM apps and agents, with datasets, prompt testing and deployment.
cons: Paid per seat and trace volume

tools.name: Transformers (Hugging Face)
tools.does: Python library that loads and runs thousands of pretrained models for text, vision and audio in a few lines.
cons: Not the fastest for production serving

tools.name: smolagents
tools.does: Small library for agents that write their actions as Python code, working with open or API models.

tools.name: Liquid AI (LFM)
tools.does: Liquid Foundation Models: small, efficient non-Transformer models (LFM2, LFM2-VL) built for phones, laptops and edge devices, plus the LEAP platform to deploy them.
tools.cost: Open models; paid API/licenses for some uses
pros: Very fast and memory-light on device

tools.name: Gradio
tools.does: Open-source Python library for building web demos and UIs for ML models in a few lines (text, image, audio, chat). Powers most Hugging Face Spaces and can share a public link or expose an app as an API.
tools.cost: Free (open source); hosting free or paid on Hugging Face Spaces
pros: Very fast to build model demos and chat UIs
Built-in Hugging Face Spaces hosting and sharing
cons: Less layout control than a full web framework
Not meant for large production apps

tools.name: Streamlit
tools.does: Open-source Python framework that turns scripts into interactive web apps and dashboards: data apps, LLM chat apps and internal tools. Owned by Snowflake; deploy on Streamlit Community Cloud, Snowflake or Hugging Face Spaces.
tools.cost: Free (open source); Community Cloud free; paid in Snowflake
pros: Pure Python, no front-end code needed
Great for data dashboards and quick LLM chat apps
cons: Reruns the whole script on each interaction, which can be slow

tools.name: Netlify
tools.does: Hosts and deploys websites and web apps from a Git repo or a folder, with serverless functions, forms and preview links for every change. Common place to publish sites built with AI app builders such as Bolt.new.
pros: Free plan is enough for personal and small sites
Deploys automatically on every Git push, with preview URLs
cons: Bandwidth and build limits on the free plan
Costs can rise with heavy traffic or many functions

tools.name: Vercel
tools.does: Hosting and deployment platform from the makers of Next.js, with serverless and edge functions, preview deployments, and the Vercel AI SDK and v0 for building AI apps.
pros: Best support for Next.js and React apps
Preview deployment for every pull request
AI SDK makes streaming chat apps easy
cons: Free Hobby plan is for non-commercial use
Usage-based costs can grow quickly at scale

tools.name: Perplexity Comet
tools.does: AI-native web browser with Perplexity built in: answers with citations, summarizes pages and can carry out multi-step tasks across tabs.
pros: Can act on pages for you

tools.name: Dia
tools.does: Chromium-based browser from the makers of Arc with an AI assistant that reads your open tabs, writes and answers questions about pages.
cons: Advanced use needs a paid plan

tools.name: Opera Neon
tools.does: Agent-first browser that can browse, fill forms and build small apps or documents for you from a prompt.
pros: Can build simple pages and docs
cons: Agent tasks can fail or need retries

tools.name: Brave Leo
tools.does: Privacy-focused AI assistant built into the Brave browser for summarizing pages, answering questions and writing.
cons: An assistant, not a full agent

tools.name: Kiro
tools.does: Agentic IDE built on spec-driven development: turns a prompt into requirements, a design and tasks, then writes the code, with hooks and steering files for team rules.
cons: Spec workflow feels slow for small fixes

tools.name: Google Antigravity
tools.does: Agent-first development platform where several coding agents work in parallel across editor, terminal and browser, managed from a mission-control view.
pros: Agents can test in a built-in browser
cons: Still new; rate limits on free use

tools.name: Cline
tools.does: Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code that plans, edits files, runs terminal commands and uses MCP tools, asking for approval at each step.
pros: Open source, works with many models
cons: Can use many tokens on big tasks

tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
tools.does: Lightweight open-source Python and TypeScript SDK for building agents with tools, handoffs between agents, guardrails and tracing.

tools.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
tools.does: Open-source .NET and Python framework that merges AutoGen and Semantic Kernel for single and multi-agent apps, with workflows, MCP and A2A support.
pros: Successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel

tools.name: Pydantic AI
tools.does: Python agent framework from the Pydantic team focused on type-safe, structured outputs, dependency injection and testable agents.

tools.name: DSPy
tools.does: Framework for programming LLM pipelines as modules and automatically optimizing their prompts and few-shot examples against a metric.
cons: Needs an eval metric and data

tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
tools.does: Open-source TypeScript toolkit for building AI apps: streaming chat, tool calling, structured output and UI hooks across many model providers.
cons: Agent features lighter than Python frameworks

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.does: C/C++ engine that runs LLMs efficiently on CPUs, Apple Silicon and GPUs using quantized GGUF models; powers many local AI apps.
cons: Not built for large multi-user serving

tools.name: SGLang
tools.does: High-performance serving engine for LLMs and vision models with fast structured output, prefix caching (RadixAttention) and multi-GPU support.
pros: Very fast, especially with shared prefixes

tools.name: Jan
tools.does: Open-source desktop app for chatting with local models offline, with an OpenAI-compatible local API server.

tools.name: GPT4All
tools.does: Free desktop app to run open models on your computer, including chatting with your local documents.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.does: Open-source library and proxy that calls 100+ model providers through one OpenAI-style API, with budgets, rate limits, logging and fallbacks.
cons: You host and maintain the proxy

tools.name: Weaviate
tools.does: Open-source vector database with hybrid (keyword plus vector) search, built-in embedding modules and a managed cloud.
cons: More to operate than simple stores

tools.name: Qdrant
tools.does: Open-source vector database written in Rust with fast filtering, quantization and a managed cloud.

tools.name: Milvus
tools.does: Open-source, highly scalable vector database for billions of vectors, with Zilliz Cloud as the managed version.

tools.name: pgvector
tools.does: PostgreSQL extension that stores embeddings and runs vector similarity search inside your existing Postgres database.
pros: Join vectors with normal SQL data
cons: Slower than dedicated stores at huge scale

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.does: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, prompt management, evaluations and cost tracking; self-host or cloud.
cons: Advanced features on paid cloud plans

tools.name: Arize Phoenix
tools.does: Open-source tool for tracing, evaluating and debugging LLM apps and agents, built on OpenTelemetry.
cons: Enterprise features in paid Arize AX

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.does: Platform for evaluating, logging and improving AI products: datasets, scorers, experiments and prompt playgrounds.

tools.name: Promptfoo
tools.does: Open-source CLI for testing prompts and models and red-teaming LLM apps for jailbreaks, prompt injection and data leaks; runs in CI.

tools.name: NeMo Guardrails
tools.does: Open-source toolkit for adding programmable guardrails to LLM apps: topic limits, jailbreak and injection checks, and safe tool use.

tools.name: Llama Guard
tools.does: Open-weight safety classifier models that label prompts and responses as safe or unsafe across standard hazard categories.
cons: Categories may not fit every policy

tools.name: Lakera Guard
tools.does: API that detects prompt injection, jailbreaks, data leakage and harmful content in LLM inputs and outputs in real time.
cons: Another vendor in the request path

tools.name: Elicit
tools.does: AI research assistant that finds academic papers, summarizes them and extracts data into tables for literature reviews.

tools.name: Consensus
tools.does: Search engine that answers questions from peer-reviewed research, showing which studies support or dispute a claim.

tools.name: DeepL
tools.does: AI translation and writing assistant for text and documents in dozens of languages, with an API for developers.

tools.name: Julius AI
tools.does: Chat with your spreadsheets and data files: it writes and runs code to clean data, analyze it and make charts.

tools.name: Intercom Fin
tools.does: AI customer-service agent that answers support questions from your help content across chat, email and voice, handing off to humans when needed.

tools.name: Sierra
tools.does: Enterprise platform for building branded AI customer-service agents that take actions such as returns and bookings.

tools.name: Khanmigo
tools.does: AI tutor and teaching assistant that guides students with questions instead of giving answers, and helps teachers plan lessons.
tools.cost: Free for teachers; paid plan for learners

tools.name: Udio
tools.does: AI music generator that creates songs with vocals from text prompts; moved toward licensed models after 2025 deals with Universal and Warner.
cons: Rules on use and downloads changed over time
Rights and usage terms need checking

tools.name: Deepgram
tools.does: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech APIs for real-time transcription and voice agents.

tools.name: AssemblyAI
tools.does: Speech AI API for transcription, speaker labels, summaries and audio intelligence features.

tools.name: Leonardo AI
tools.does: Image and video generation platform for artwork, game assets and marketing visuals, with fine-tuned models and editing tools.
pros: Good for game and concept art
cons: Daily token limits on free plan

tools.name: Nano Banana (Gemini image)
tools.does: Gemini image generation and editing model, popular for consistent characters and precise edits from text instructions.
pros: Available in the Gemini app and API

tools.name: Luma Dream Machine
tools.does: Video generation from text and images with realistic motion, plus tools to extend, edit and restyle clips.

tools.name: Meshy
tools.does: Creates textured 3D models from text or images for games, 3D printing and AR, with export to common formats.

tools.name: Make
tools.does: Visual no-code automation platform (formerly Integromat) for connecting apps, with AI modules and agents.
pros: Cheaper than Zapier for many tasks

tools.name: Microsoft Power Automate
tools.does: Workflow automation for Microsoft 365 and other apps, with desktop RPA and Copilot to build flows from plain language.

tools.name: Granola
tools.does: AI notepad for meetings: transcribes your computer audio without a bot joining the call and turns your rough notes into clean summaries.
pros: Combines your notes with the transcript

tools.name: OpenArt
tools.does: All-in-one creative platform that gives access to many image, video and audio models (such as Nano Banana, GPT Image, Seedream, Kling and Veo) in one place, with editing, inpainting, consistent characters and custom model training.
pros: Many top image and video models in one subscription
Consistent characters and custom model training
cons: Credit-based plans; free credits are limited
Quality depends on the model you pick

tools.name: OmniRoute
tools.does: Open-source, self-hosted AI gateway that puts one OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint in front of many model providers, with smart routing and automatic fallback across subscription, API-key, cheap and free models; works with coding tools such as Claude Code, Cursor and Cline.
pros: Automatic fallback keeps coding agents running
cons: You install and maintain it yourself
Mostly one main maintainer; check forks and docs carefully

tools.name: Xiaomi MiMo
tools.does: Xiaomi's MIT-licensed open-weight models for reasoning, coding and agents. MiMo-V2-Flash (December 2025) is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 309B total and 15B active parameters; newer V2.5 and V2.6 versions followed. Available on Hugging Face, MiMo Studio and an API.
pros: Strong coding and agent results for its cost
cons: Large models need serious GPUs to self-host

tools.name: NVIDIA Nemotron
tools.does: NVIDIA's family of open models released together with open training data and recipes. Nemotron 3 (from December 2025) comes in Nano, Super and Ultra sizes: efficient hybrid Mixture-of-Experts models built for agents.
pros: Weights, data and recipes are open
Optimized for NVIDIA GPUs and NIM
cons: NVIDIA model license terms to check

tools.name: MiniMax
tools.does: Chinese AI lab whose open-weight MiniMax-M2 series (from October 2025; 230B total, 10B active parameters) is strong at coding and agentic tool use at low cost; it also powers the MiniMax Agent app.
pros: Low API price for strong coding
cons: Weaker than leaders on some general tasks

tools.name: gpt-oss
tools.does: OpenAI's open-weight reasoning models (August 2025): gpt-oss-120b runs on a single 80 GB GPU and gpt-oss-20b on devices with 16 GB of memory. Apache 2.0 license.

tools.name: Llama
tools.does: Meta's widely used family of open-weight models, from small on-device models to large multimodal ones; the base for many fine-tuned models.

tools.name: Gemma
tools.does: Google's lightweight open models built from Gemini research, including multimodal and on-device versions.
pros: Runs well on laptops and phones

tools.name: Phi
tools.does: Microsoft's small language models trained on high-quality data, strong at reasoning for their size and suited to edge devices.
pros: Very capable for its small size
cons: Less world knowledge than big models

tools.name: OLMo
tools.does: Fully open language models: weights, training data, code and logs are all published, which makes them ideal for research and transparency.

tools.name: IBM Granite
tools.does: IBM's Apache 2.0 open models for business use: language, code, embedding and safety models, available on watsonx and Hugging Face.

tools.name: GLM
tools.does: Open-weight GLM models from Zhipu AI for reasoning, coding and agents, plus the Z.ai chat app and API.
cons: Large models are costly to self-host

tools.name: Hailuo AI
tools.does: MiniMax's video generator for text-to-video and image-to-video, known for realistic motion and good prompt following.
